mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the preceding 60 days reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for 60 days in a row
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS increases, or IC > 0.05 over 1-year horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer confidence and accelerates S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to expectations of sustained economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 by more than 10,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when PAYEMS spikes occur, or IC < -0.1 over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of GDP demand component (GDPC1) to potential GDP (INDPRO) exceeds 110% for two consecutive quarters, it indicates over-heating demand that drives S&P 500 forward returns positive in the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 / INDPRO > 1.10 for two consecutive quarterly observations
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 over 1-year horizon during such trigger periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of 2% or more for three months suggests supply constraints that raise uncertainty and depress S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >= 2% monthly for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during such supply shocks, or IC > 0.08 over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, it triggers a risk-off sentiment that produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: IC > 0.1 over 6 months during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a rise above 4.5% creates a volatility spike that is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% then above 4.5% within the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive during such transitions, or IC < -0.15 over 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signal a shift toward tighter policy expectations that suppress S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when inflation accelerates, or IC > 0.09 over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A negative interaction between industrial production (INDPRO) and manufacturing activity (not available in the provided proxies; use RSAFS as proxy for manufacturing) indicates supply chain dislocation that precedes negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 and RSAFS < 100 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: IC > 0.12 over 1-year horizon during dislocation events.
